title: 1987 AMC 8 Problem 21
statement:
Suppose \(n^\ast\) means \(\dfrac1n,\) the reciprocal of \(n.\) For example, \(5^\ast = \dfrac15.\) How many of the following four statements are true?

\[\mathrm{(i)}\quad 3^\ast + 6^\ast = 9^\ast\]

\[\mathrm{(ii)}\quad 6^\ast - 4^\ast = 2^\ast\]

\[\mathrm{(iii)}\quad 2^\ast \cdot 6^\ast = 12^\ast\]

\[\mathrm{(iv)}\quad 10^\ast \div 2^\ast = 5^\ast\]

solutions.text:
\(\mathrm{(i)}\) \(\dfrac13 + \dfrac16 = \dfrac12,\) but \(9^\ast = \dfrac19,\) so false. \(\mathrm{(ii)}\) \(\dfrac16 - \dfrac14 = -\dfrac{1}{12},\) but \(2^\ast = \dfrac12,\) so false.

\(\mathrm{(iii)}\) \(\dfrac12 \cdot \dfrac16 = \dfrac{1}{12} = 12^\ast,\) true. \(\mathrm{(iv)}\) \(\dfrac{1}{10} \div \dfrac12 = \dfrac15 = 5^\ast,\) true.

So exactly \(2\) of the statements are true.

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: Replace each \(n^\ast\) with \(\dfrac1n\) and test the two sides of each statement
